chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Sneaking in to hear Johnny Hodges with Ellington
summary: At fourteen he talks a doorman into letting him sit on the bandstand steps to hear his idol Johnny Hodges.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So when Duke Ellington came to town, I... I was determined to hear Johnny Hodges. So they were playing a dance down at the White armory, they was playing...at the White auditorium downtown. I was about fourteen. So I went down there. And they had this big guy, you know, like the security guy by the front, by the door, you know... So I went up to him and I told him...I said that I was studying music, and Johnny Hodges, my idol, was playing with the Duke Ellington band, and I really wanted to hear him, you know. And he thought it over. [LAUGHS] He stood there and he thought it over. But, uh... He knew I really wanted to hear the band, you know, and so... He took a chance on is job, really. So he opened the door and he pulled me over to the door, and he says, "Now, look. Do you see those steps up

there?" -- [the steps by the bandstand.] He said, "Do you see those steps up there? You go up there and sit on those steps, and don't you move!" [LAUGHS HEARTILY] I said, "Okay," you know, and that's what I did. And every now and then, he would check up to see if I was still sitting on those steps. And that's where I first heard Johnny Hodges and the Duke Ellington Orchestra. I didn't get a chance to say anything to any of them or anything, but I sat there on those steps and heard that band. And after it was all over, I left and I thanked him, you know, and went home. But I was determined to hear Johnny Hodges play, you know.
Oh, I was just thrilled to death to hear that band, to hear Johnny play, you know. Yeah, it was really-really-really something special to me.
